key_insight: ADSMoE identified four Alzheimer's disease subtypes with distinct biological and clinical characteristics by learning from incomplete multimodal data.
clinical_relevance: The findings may support future Alzheimer's disease stratification and biomarker discovery, but do not establish clinical utility or treatment guidance.
method: Uses a mixture-of-experts transformer autoencoder to learn multimodal disease signatures.
A flexible encoder accommodates varying combinations of available modalities.
A subtype-specific decoder captures complementary disease characteristics through expert specialization.
evidence_signal: Across 5,422 participants in three cohorts, ADSMoE was trained on ADNI and externally validated in NACC and UKB without retraining, with consistent subtype-associated characteristics reported.
watch_item: The abstract does not report quantitative validation metrics or demonstrate that subtype assignment improves clinical decisions.
paper_title: ADSMoE: A mixture-of-experts-based transformer autoencoder for discovering multimodal Alzheimer's disease subtypes
